name: Flucloxacillin
reviewed_by: William Gregory M. Rivero, MD, FPCP, DPSN
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero

usual_adult_dose.indication: Staphylococcal infections (oral, adults and children over 10)
usual_adult_dose.dose: 250 to 500 mg three times daily, 1 hour before or 2 hours after food
Up to 8 g/day in divided doses every 6 to 8 hours
1 to 2 g intravenously at induction, then 500 mg every 6 hours for up to 72 hours

key_interactions.effect: High anion gap metabolic acidosis (5-oxoproline), mainly with severe kidney impairment, sepsis or malnutrition.
key_interactions.action: Use with caution; monitor acid–base status.
Monitor voriconazole levels; dose increase may be needed.

serious: Cholestatic jaundice and hepatitis (may be delayed up to 2 months after stopping; most fatal cases in people over 50 or with serious underlying disease)
Stevens-Johnson syndrome, toxic epidermal necrolysis, acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis
Convulsions with high intravenous doses in kidney failure
Hypokalemia; high anion gap metabolic acidosis with paracetamol

contraindications: Previous flucloxacillin-associated jaundice or hepatic dysfunction
monitoring: Liver tests in long courses and if jaundice appears; never re-challenge after flucloxacillin jaundice; kidney function in long courses
Acid–base status if combined with paracetamol in at-risk patients

pk.bioavailability: Well absorbed; absorption halved when taken with food
pk.excretion_renal_pct: 20% to 50% of an oral dose in urine

sources.citation: Pinewood Laboratories Ltd. (2023). Flucillin (flucloxacillin) capsules 500 mg [Summary of product characteristics, licence PA0281/031/005; text revised May 2023]. Health Products Regulatory Authority (Ireland).

revision_log.change: Hepatotoxicity profile (delayed onset, deaths mostly >50 y or serious disease); liver tests; no re-challenge.
